lesson.title: The Open Court Is Not Always Open
lesson.hook: You hit toward empty space just as the opponent is already arriving there.
lesson.tomorrow: Next time an opponent sprints, notice whether playing behind them becomes available.

pro.label: Jankovic's coach, Indian Wells 2010
pro.moment: At a changeover, Chip Brooks told Jankovic: "You're being very successful when you're hitting behind her; when she's running to the open court, she's hitting winners."
pro.read: Make their run part of your target.

drill.name: Behind the run
drill.how: Play out points. A point you win by hitting behind a running opponent counts double.

steps.name: Defender running right
steps.sit: You have a comfortable short forehand. Watch where the defender is running before you choose.
steps.q: Which target makes them stop and turn?
opts: Back to the left, behind them
steps.payoff: Behind a runner, they have to brake and turn.
steps.principle: When a player is moving, the empty space is where they're arriving.
steps.why: They're already sprinting right, so the empty side is where they'll be. Behind them, they have to stop and change direction, which costs more time than the distance.
steps.take: They're running right? Play behind them — make them brake and turn.

lines.A: They were already heading there — they get it back; rally on.
lines.B: They have to brake and turn — too late. Wrong-footed.
lines.C: High through the middle gives them time to recover.
lines.D: They run the drop down — and their reply gets past you.

steps.name: Defender holds left
steps.sit: Same short ball, but this time the defender stays left and sets their feet.
opts: Short drop in front of them
steps.payoff: They're not running, so there's no 'behind'. Make them travel.
steps.principle: Behind only works on a runner. Against a player standing still, hit to the far space.
steps.why: They haven't moved, so there's no momentum to beat. The wide right side is simply the longest way for them to go.
steps.take: Not running? Hit to the space they have to travel to.

lines.A: Behind a player who isn't moving is straight into their hitting zone.
lines.B: They run the drop down — and their reply gets past you.
lines.C: A loop through the middle — the rally just starts again.
lines.D: The right side makes them travel — too far to reach.

steps.name: Backhand, defender running left
steps.sit: Now it comes to your backhand, and the defender is running left.
steps.q: Which shot goes against their run?
opts: Down the line, to the left
steps.payoff: Same read on the other wing: behind the run.
steps.principle: Read the run, not the side of the court.
steps.why: They're travelling left, so the right side is behind them, whichever wing you hit from.
steps.take: Read the run, not the side: play behind it, whichever wing.

lines.A: Crosscourt behind their run — they can't turn in time.
lines.B: Down the line is where they're going — they get there; rally on.
lines.C: Firm through the middle — they recover and the rally goes on.
lines.D: High to the left, where they're heading — they're there early.
